Over the years I have developed many simple and fun ways of explaining and practicing English grammar and vocabulary. In my lessons with younger students, I use songs, role plays, and games to make my lessons rich and exciting. In my lessons with adult students, I use news articles, debates, literature, and advanced discussion questions, to help you take your English to the next level. Practice makes perfect, and I truly believe that consistent, enjoyable practice is the most important thing for language learners.  As a language lover myself, I bring to the classroom boundless enthusiasm and a strong awareness of the problems that language learners might encounter. 

If you buy a package, I am available to help you between lessons with any difficulties you might have. I'm known for being a diligent and tireless teacher. pro_course_detail.title: Story Time!
pro_course_detail.description:
In this lesson, we will read short stories and/or books together. Stories are a great way to keep us interested and engaged in learning. We will alternate reading in order to work on your pronunciation while you are reading and your listening while I am reading. We will slow down and focus on tricky grammatical structures as well. The key is to make sure that we get the MEANING. I will also have noted some key vocabulary which towards the end of the lesson you will try to use by forming sentences. Generally the books will be in the young adult/teen category of books. (i.e. Bridge to Tarabithia/The Lion, The Witch and The Wardrobe/The Little Prince) but I am certainly open to suggestions as well. Come on! Let's read!

Note: I do recommend a package for these lessons so that we can complete the story or novel and devote more time to understanding its meaning and themes.

We can also find synonyms and other words for you to use to expand your vocabulary. Basically this class is whatever YOU want it to be. Whatever you'd like to talk about is the direction we will go. pro_course_detail.title: Images
pro_course_detail.description:
This lesson is all about images, images, images. A visual approach to learning languages helps us bypass translating from our native language into the one we are learning. We learn a word and it's connected directly to the image thus eliminating the "middle man" so to say. 

In this lesson we will look at images and you will describe the situation in the picture as best as possible. Not settling for a rough approximation, we will find the best words and vocabulary to accurately describe what is going on. After that, we will get more specific and learn the words for specific objects in the picture. As you may well know, there are truly a lot of words in every language. This becomes very clear when you try to comprehensively describe an image, which often times has many elements to it. Is it blurry or in-focus? What are the people doing in the background? Where does it take place? What is the mood of the photo? How would you describe the expressions on the peoples faces?

These lessons are extremely fun. Especially in follow up lessons where we take the first few minutes to review the previous images and vocabulary. The specific vocabulary you had learned can be on the tip of your tongue! It's fun to see which words you can remember.

Hi! Thanks for checking out what a lesson like me would be like. 

ENGLISH:
The trial lesson will mostly be a conversation between the two of us. First, I will ask you some questions about yourself and your experience with English. Then I will tell you a little about myself. After that we will work together to make a plan for how you can best proceed learning English. I will be taking notes throughout this process about your English, what you are doing well, and areas we could work together to improve. If this sounds like what you need, feel free to try it out!

CHICHEWA:
As most people start Chichewa from scratch, the trial lesson in this case will be the first lesson in the Chichewa curriculum: greetings. By the end of it, you will know how to properly greet people formally and informally at certain times of the day. If you choose to continue after this lesson, the format will be similar but on different topics. I will send you a word document and the PowerPoint we used after each lesson, as well as a vocabulary list of the most important vocabulary for the following week if you'd like to learn it ahead of time (helpful, but not necessary, because I try my best to keep the vocabulary on the screen while we work on grammar).

pro_course_detail.title: Conversation Practice
pro_course_detail.description:
This lesson is exactly what it sounds like—the opportunity to practice your English! In our first lesson, I will ask random questions designed to get to know one another better and keep the conversation flowing. I will not interrupt you to make corrections, unless you specifically request that. The lesson is an entirely natural conversation. Throughout the lesson, I will be typing what you're doing well and what could be improved into a Word Document. I will write down all the grammatical mistakes and mistakes in pronunciation that you make, along with corrections. I will send you this document after each lesson.

For all remaining lessons, I will ask if you have a topic you would like to discuss. If not, would you like me to choose one? Or would you rather discuss anything that comes up? Most of the time, I speak with students about news articles in an area they are interested in, but it is entirely up to you what you want to talk about!

I am from the United States and speak with a General American/Standard American English accent (GA/SAE).

pro_course_detail.title: English Grammar
pro_course_detail.description: In this lesson, we will work on topics in English grammar that you are struggling with. After we identify some areas of weakness for you (together), we will spend some time discussing how to work through them. Then, working from either a shared Google Doc (or a Word Document which I will send to you after the lesson). I usually explain things and draw tables or diagrams before working through some practice exercises together with you, and then ask you to have a conversation with me on a topic that will help practice the grammatical topic that you have been learning. I will provide feedback at the end of the lesson as well as in the document that I send to you afterwards.

pro_course_detail.title: Beginner's Chichewa for English Speakers
pro_course_detail.description:
Moni nonse! This lesson is for English speakers with no background in Chichewa at all. We will spend time discussing some basic vocabulary and the structure of the language. You will be speaking basic Chichewa in the first lesson. If you choose to continue with more lessons, we will discuss the many interesting facets of Chichewa, like noun classes, locatives, and extremely easy verb tenses.

How do I know Chichewa? I spent almost 3 years in Malawi teaching English to secondary school students. Additionally, my partner is Malawian, a native speaker, so I get a lot of practice in this language. Although I am not a native speaker, I became so fluent that I wrote a 200 page book in the language, which is under consideration for publication in Malawi.

Chichewa is called Chinyanja or Nyanja in Zambia. Chinyanja and Chichewa are generally considered to be the same language but there are some minor differences between them. The variety I speak is Malawian, specifically the dialect from the Kasungu and Lilongwe area, which is considered the standard dialect.

If you have some background in another Bantu language, like Swahili or Zulu, learning Chichewa will be very easy.

For the initial lessons, I follow the same format, though I adapt to each individual students' vocabulary needs depending on why they're learning the language. I have pre-made Quizlet decks with the vocabulary for each lesson I'll share with you, as well as optional post-lesson worksheets. Here is the general structure of lessons we cover:

1. Greetings
2. Pronouns and Verb Tenses
3. Tenses and Tones
4. Questions
5. Intro to Noun Classes (Mu-A Nouns)
6. Chi-Zi Nouns
7. More Verb Tenses
8. Possessives
9. I-Zi Nouns
10. Review Lesson [No Deck]

These lessons tend to be more grammar-heavy than my English lessons (though I can modify that if desired). Post-lesson 10, lessons are more flexible and I include more 'topical' content and themes (i.e. travel, shopping, weddings, funerals, folk tales, etc.)

pro_course_detail.title: Writing Help and Review
pro_course_detail.description:
(Note: Please do not book this lesson without either sending me a document or messaging me to send you an essay prompt. This is so we can review your essay (which is already written) at the time of the lesson. We can also work on resumes and cover letters.

In this lesson, I will either share my screen or work with you to edit an essay you've written on Google Docs. We will work together to fix grammar, punctuation, and spelling mistakes. We can work on anything. In the past students have worked on essays, while others have simply reviewed the e-mails they've written for work. If it's written down, we can focus on it in this lesson.

You should send me a Word document containing your essay and I will then share my screen with you and read your essay out loud, and note where I see mistakes. When we meet, I will highlight the mistakes in a different color and work with you to correct them. At the end of the lesson, I will send you back your edited essay(s). You can write essays on any topic, and it can be practice essays you've written for TOEFL or IELTS. If you would like for me to provide a topic for you to write about, please message me after booking the lesson and I will provide you with at least 2. In general, it is possible to work on 1-2 essays per hour, depending on your level and the essay length.

pro_course_detail.title: English Literature
pro_course_detail.description: In this course, we will discuss English-language literature. I have a set list of short stories, novels, and poetry that I will send to you for you to choose from to read prior to our initial lesson. You can also select something that isn't on the list! I'll then come up with discussion questions for us to talk about during the lesson. Apart from that, I treat my feedback like my other English lessons -- I will write down any sentence you make that has a mistake and note corrections in it. I will organize these corrections by theme and send them to you in a Word document (along with the discussion questions) and any new vocabulary we discuss.

pro_course_detail.title: American English Pronunciation Workshop
pro_course_detail.description: These lessons are designed to focus explicitly on pronunciation and have you sounding more like a native speaker of American English. Many pronunciation problems can be traced back to the way you pronounce words in your native language. In these lessons, we will discuss the pronunciation rules of your own native language before discussing how to work on the different rules of the English language. We generally also learn the IPA (International Phonetic Alphabet) sounds relevant to English. Because English has so many vowel sounds compared to many other languages, this is often essential in distinguishing between similar-sounding words to non-native speakers (like 'live' and 'leave,' for example). Some people find this lesson type very technical and it can be overwhelming for beginners, but intermediate and advanced learners usually find it helpful.

pro_course_detail.title: Let's talk Business!
pro_course_detail.description:
We all yearn to understand and/or be better understood in the workplace. Why choose Coach David? My clients tell me they suffer from “teacher syndrome”, they complain about not being well understood, have listening issues, having low confidence when communicating in English and etc..

What does Coach David do?  He certainly doesn’t teach English. Everyone has a story. Share your story with coach David and you are sure to immediately feel improvement.  In Business English, we say “this is half the battle”...for “we now feel comfortable enough to drastically start improving our BusinessSpeak.

“BusinessSpeak" is nothing more than “an artful and bastardized English” spoken in a manner in which we immediately feel comfortable with one another in the workplace.  Business English helps create meaningful and trusting relationships.

Empathy and portraying a positive spirit is also a key ingredient.  As you are to make it big, you are welcome to join me in your English enhancement from my vast business acumen.

BusinessSpeak contains a host of business idioms, jargon, lingo, sarcasm, negotiation skills and even a few jokes. These being most necessary tools to be in one's language arsenal.  iTalki in conjunction with mediums such as Skype and Zoom are great platforms to fine-tune ones work related spoken business skills!

In the workplace, it is imperative that one "strikes a cord"...meaning one sparks emotional energy in conversation.  This expression with confidence, helps in dealing with our work associates and/or clients that we all rely upon.

"The sizzle sells the steak" or in other words "business and technical knowledge only play a small part". The power happens in the way we say what we say.

As a well experienced serial entrepreneur and work-life coach, Coach David looks much forward in helping you in your fruitful journey of your self-confidence build out.
